name: Jessica Pratt
label: Mexican Summer
lede: She recorded her first songs on analogue tape in 2007, sat on them for five years, and ended up on a Chanel runway, a late-night couch and an A$AP Rocky single.

eras.title: A kid in Redding with a borrowed guitar
eras.text: Pratt grew up in Redding, California, in a house where the stereo ran from Tim Buckley to X. Everything she would later release was being made in a bedroom, for nobody.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician) · Stereogum: Q&A Jessica Pratt
years.h: Jessica Pratt is born in Redding, California
years.p: Her mother, an astrologer, raised her on Tim Buckley, X and the Gun Club.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Pratt grew up in Redding with her mother, who played her a wide run of records: Tim Buckley, X, the Gun Club. She was, in Stereogum's telling, technically homeschooled, though she has said it was largely because she had no interest in school.

years.h: Her brother's Stratocaster, and T. Rex's Electric Warrior
years.p: She inherited the Fender and learned to play along with the 1971 album Electric Warrior.
years.xp: By 16 she was recording songs at home on her mother's equipment, according to Wikipedia. The four-track habit she started then would define her first two records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (album) · Exclaim!: Jessica Pratt Talks
years.h: The tapes: songs she would not release for five years
years.p: Pratt records the songs that will become her debut album on analogue tape, in a friend of a friend's studio.
years.xp: She told Exclaim! the studio belonged to a friend's friend who "just had some free time". The recordings then sat, unreleased, until a roommate's brother passed them to someone with a label idea.

eras.title: A label built for one record
eras.text: In San Francisco, a roommate's brother carried her tapes to Tim Presley of White Fence. He started Birth Records to put them out.

q: He really did it out of the goodness of his heart.
years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician) · Exclaim!: Jessica Pratt Talks
years.h: Tim Presley starts Birth Records to release her tapes
years.p: [[Tim Presley|25f6404b-4738-48a2-b1e0-465b7430fb93]] of [[White Fence|68548de4-c045-426a-9745-b52a8a22d2d2]] heard the demos through her then-boyfriend and founded a label for the job.
years.xp:
Pratt had lived in San Francisco with Presley's brother as her roommate for three years. Presley heard the recordings and, she told Exclaim!, "did it out of the goodness of his heart".

Birth Records, Wikipedia says, was founded specifically to release her music.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (album) · Stereogum: Q&A Jessica Pratt · Drag City: Jessica Pratt
years.h: Jessica Pratt: 500 copies, gone in two weeks
years.p: The debut on Birth Records sold out its first pressing fast and got Pitchfork, Consequence of Sound and PopMatters writing about a singer nobody had heard of.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Pitchfork rated it 7.5 and Metacritic averaged 78 from seven critics. The Boston Globe compared its fingerpicked intimacy to Sibylle Baier. PopMatters was more mixed, finding the production made some words hard to make out.

Pratt told Stereogum that her mother died a couple of years before the release, and that she later found from tape dates that she had recorded "Strange Melody" six days after. Drag City lists the record as 2011; Wikipedia gives November 2012.

eras.title: Drag City, and a bedroom in Silverlake
eras.text: She moved to Los Angeles, bought a Tascam, and made the record she calls her first real debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Your Own Love Again · Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician)
years.h: "Back, Baby" lands on Pitchfork's best tracks of 2014
years.p: The track from her second album placed No. 82 on Pitchfork's list of the year's 100 best tracks.
years.xp: The song would have a second life: Troye Sivan sampled it on his 2023 album Something to Give Each Other.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Your Own Love Again · Stereogum: Q&A Jessica Pratt · Exclaim!: Jessica Pratt Talks
years.h: On Your Own Love Again on Drag City, cut on a 4-track
years.p: She recorded it on a Tascam 424 Portastudio in her small Silverlake bedroom, then called it her first real debut.
years.xp:
Pratt told Stereogum she was "pretty sad and lonely" in Los Angeles while making it. Will Canzoneri added organ and clavinet; the title came from what she calls a "psychic dream phrase" that arrived while she was writing the closing song, per Exclaim!.

Pitchfork gave it 8.1 and Metacritic averaged 79 from 24 reviews, according to Wikipedia. Pitchfork later put it at No. 85 on its list of the 2010s' best albums.

years.h: Opening for Beach House, Panda Bear and José González
years.p: Pratt toured on the back of the Drag City record as both headliner and support act, and played Pitchfork Music Festival 2015.

eras.title: A real studio, finally
eras.text: Mexican Summer and City Slang brought her into a proper studio with producer Al Carlson, and the sound came into focus.

years.src: Wikipedia: Quiet Signs · Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician)
years.h: Quiet Signs: first studio record, first for Mexican Summer
years.p: Produced by [[Al Carlson|50f1661d-aeff-4d72-b4e1-6046d39675c8]], it reached No. 4 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and No. 15 on the UK Independent Albums chart, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
Pitchfork rated it 8.4 and Metacritic averaged 84. Pitchfork described single "This Time Around" as a tropicalia take on a Christmas song, or a 60s jukebox standard in an off-season beach-town diner.

City Slang co-released it in Europe.

years.h: Pitchfork puts On Your Own Love Again at No. 85 of the decade
years.p: The 2015 four-track record ranked among the site's best albums of the 2010s.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician) · AOL: Jessica Pratt Dreams Big
years.p: Pratt wrote the next record through the pandemic, in a long gap before anything came out.
years.xp: By the time Here in the Pitch arrived it was her fourth record in 12 years and first in five, per AOL's review. Her partner, keyboardist Matt McDermott, played on it.

years.h: Troye Sivan samples "Back, Baby" on a major-label pop record
years.p: The 2014 single from Pratt's second album turns up on Sivan's Something to Give Each Other.

eras.title: Here in the Pitch
eras.text: Orchestral touches, a runway and a Colbert spot: her biggest year was built on a 27-minute record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Here in the Pitch · AOL: Jessica Pratt Dreams Big
years.h: Here in the Pitch: the fourth album, nine songs, 27 minutes
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.8 and Best New Music, then ranked it No. 3 on its list of the 50 best albums of 2024.
years.xp:
Pratt made it at Gary's Electric in Brooklyn with Al Carlson, Matt McDermott on keys, [[Spencer Zahn|2bd4b13a-afcb-428d-9ee4-61ee8092c28c]] on bass and [[Mauro Refosco|a1659091-7fba-403b-bc78-89e8b2651d79]] on percussion; Ryley Walker, Peter Mudge and Alex Goldberg also contributed. Pitchfork's Jeremy D. Larson called her "music's greatest horologist" (Wikipedia's reception box).

Metacritic averaged 90 from 14 critics. Paste gave it 9.5, The Line of Best Fit 8. The album also placed No. 6 at Stereogum and No. 5 at Uncut in year-end lists.

years.src: Wikipedia: Here in the Pitch · BrooklynVegan: Jessica Pratt
years.h: Dark California, as she sings it
years.p: She said the songs drew on the hippie-era Los Angeles of Manson and Pet Sounds, the dark side of the Californian dream.
years.xp: She told the New York Times she loves a "micro era" of 60s pop where the production feels "atmospheric like a snow globe". BrooklynVegan's interview covered her love of Pet Sounds and the Manson-era setting.

years.h: "Life Is" closes Chanel's haute couture show
years.p: Her lead single is used as the closing music of the Fall-Winter 2024/25 couture presentation.

years.h: Late-night debut on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert
years.p: Pratt plays "Life Is" on Colbert's show, a late-night television debut.

q: a Portishead meets Stevie Nicks vibe
years.h: A$AP Rocky asks her to sing on "Highjack"
years.p: [[A$AP Rocky|25b7b584-d952-4662-a8b9-dd8cdfbfeb64]] told Zane Lowe that was why he wanted Pratt, and had [[Jon Batiste|a2a72dba-3a08-43c4-859c-4c7f5fcc9599]] add a soulful outro.
years.xp: "Highjack" was billed as the lead single for Rocky's Don't Be Dumb, but per Wikipedia it was left off the finished record. Stereogum noted Pratt sings the second half; Hitkidd and Greg Kurstin are among the producers.

eras.title: After the pitch
eras.text: She toured the record and other musicians started covering her, including the whole debut.

years.h: Asher White covers the entire debut album
years.p: White released a full-album cover of Jessica Pratt through Joyful Noise, sending new listeners back to the 2012 original.
